facts.claim: An A2A agent publishes an agent card, a small structured file at a fixed address on its domain that names the agent, describes it, and lists its address, version, capabilities, input and output types and skills (A2A specification 1.0.0).

An A2A task moves through states including submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed and canceled; completed, failed, canceled and rejected end it, while input-required and auth-required pause it until the agent that sent it answers (A2A specification 1.0.0).
The A2A specification’s latest release is version 1.0.0, after 0.1.0, 0.2.6 and 0.3.0.
The Linux Foundation launched the Agent2Agent project on 23 June 2025, starting from the protocol Google created, with AWS, Cisco, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow.

Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) in September 2025 with more than 60 organisations: a person signs an intent mandate with price limits and timing up front, and a cart mandate fixes the exact items and price; both are cryptographically signed.
Google describes AP2 as usable as an extension of the A2A protocol and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
On 28 April 2026 the FIDO Alliance said Google’s AP2 and Mastercard’s Verifiable Intent would be developed further in its Payments Technical Working Group.

AP2’s own site lists release v0.2 and the FIDO donation, and names a checkout mandate (the items and terms agreed with the merchant) and a payment mandate (the payment against one card or account), each signed so that any change shows.

AP2’s specification (v0.2) has two modes: with the person present, they see and approve the exact checkout and payment; with the person away, they approve limits up front and the agent signs an order that fits them, and the limits should expire as soon as the task allows.

Stripe and OpenAI released the Agentic Commerce Protocol on 29 September 2025; its Shared Payment Token lets an agent start a payment without seeing the card, and is scoped to one merchant and one basket total.

The Agentic Commerce Protocol’s delegated payment spec gives each handed-over card an allowance for one use only, up to a maximum amount, in one currency, for one checkout at one merchant, until an expiry time (OpenAI’s docs, checked 2026-10-30).

The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), co-developed by Google, Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Stripe and others by its own site’s list, covers shopping from discovery to checkout and works with AP2, A2A and MCP.
The Model Context Protocol connects AI applications to outside tools and data with a standard message format; its current specification is dated 2026-07-28.
On WebArena’s realistic websites the best GPT-4-based agent finished 14.41% of tasks end to end, against 78.24% for people (Zhou et al., 2023).
Instructions hidden in data an AI application reads can steer it without the attacker ever talking to it: indirect prompt injection (Greshake et al., 2023).

Researchers attacking a working shopping agent built on AP2 (with Gemini 2.5 Flash) found that simple hostile prompts reliably changed what it did, from how it ranked products to leaking the user’s private data (Debi, Zhu and Sen Gupta, 2026).
